You can leave this screen; the check continues in the background.
Cancelled. Feeds not checked keep their HTTP URL.

Each http:// feed is fetched once over HTTPS with normal certificate checks. Only feeds that return the same RSS/Atom feed over HTTPS are switched to HTTPS. Feed, categories, articles and read/saved state stay as they are. Anything else keeps its HTTP URL. Allowing HTTP for the remaining feeds is a separate setting.
Check HTTPS support of HTTP feeds
There are %1$d HTTP feeds. Check whether they work over HTTPS and switch the ones that do?
HTTPS returned a web page, not a feed
Feeds left on HTTP are fetched only if you allow HTTP in Settings.
Changed to HTTPS %1$d · not changed %2$d · not checked %3$d
old RSS 0.91 feed that declares a DTD, which Folirel does not read
Waiting after a failure or for the server\'s Retry-After. A manual refresh retries an ordinary failure now; a server wait is respected.
The last update stopped while fetching this feed (time limit or stopped). Retry unfinished feeds.
Still being fetched for another update.
http:// feed: not fetched while HTTP is not allowed. Check HTTPS support, or allow HTTP in Settings.
The last update ended before reaching this feed (time limit). It goes first next time.

Use "Revalidate and refetch" when a normal refresh does not bring changes: stored validators are not sent and caches are asked to revalidate. Articles and read/saved state are kept. A server or CDN may still return old content.

Limit: about %1$d. Stored now: %2$d. Old read, unsaved articles to remove now: %3$d; the same cleanup runs after updates. Unread and saved articles are never removed (now: %4$d). Removed articles are not added again as unread.
Remaining: %1$d, above the limit because unread or saved articles are kept (%2$d).
Old OPML files may still contain http:// feeds. They are not fetched unless HTTP is allowed. The check below switches only feeds verified over HTTPS.
Applies at the next app start. Clearing or shrinking the cache never touches subscriptions, read or saved state.
Articles to keep on the device
Not a fetch limit: every article a feed returns is stored. Only old read, unsaved articles above this number are removed, after your confirmation.
At most every 30 minutes, with the same network rule as automatic updates.
Feeds: %1$d · last result OK %2$d · failed %3$d · HTTP pending %4$d · waiting %5$d · unfinished %6$d
Feeds still on http://: %1$d. They are not fetched unless HTTP is allowed.
Redirected to another site; not confirmed as the same feed (allowing HTTP lets the check compare)

Magazine, Masonry and Bento use this many columns at most. Automatic follows the screen width and text size. A number that would make headlines too narrow to read (small window, large text) is reduced; text is never shrunk to keep columns.

resources.string: A failure does not prove that a site is closed: 404/410 can also mean the address moved, and connection, busy or server errors often pass. Articles, saved and read state and categories stay on the device (saved articles remain under Saved). You can undo right after, and subscribe again later from the list. Importing an older OPML would subscribe these feeds again.
This file contains feeds you unsubscribed. Importing subscribes them again and fetches them:
Address changed. The feed keeps its articles, categories and read/saved state.
That address already belongs to another subscription (%s). Nothing was merged.
The feed changed in the meantime. Nothing was changed.
Looks on the feed\'s own site for RSS/Atom links and checks that each one is a real feed. Nothing is chosen or changed for you.
Search the web by feed name
Opens your device search with the feed name and \"RSS\" when you tap it. Nothing is sent from here otherwise. Paste an address you find below to check it.
No app on this device can run a web search.
Site or feed address you found
Read the site page and listed the feed links it declares.
The address is itself a feed.
No site address is known for this feed. Enter one below.

The page could not be read.
No RSS/Atom links were found there.
no articles in common, different title: check before using

The feed keeps its articles, categories and read/saved state. Articles of the new address are matched by their own ids and links, so some may appear again as new. Older OPML files that name the old address still find this feed.
This changes the default layout for every category that has no layout of its own.

Articles whose title or summary contain one of these words are left out of the lists. Nothing is deleted, marked as read or saved, and nothing is fetched differently. Turn the filter off or remove a word to see them again.
This word is already in the list.
A word can have 64 characters at most.

No articles match the period or the hidden keywords.
Tab order (the hierarchy is not changed)

Only the order is reset. Pins and the display settings of each category stay.
No subscribed feed, so no tab
A number you choose is reduced when it does not fit the window or the text size.
Reset the display of this category
Only the layout, the arrangement and the columns go back to the defaults. Pin, order, subscriptions and read state stay.
Applies to %1$s only. Other categories keep their own layout.
This is the default for every category. A category can use its own layout from the display panel of the home screen.
Do not ask again on metered networks
Confirm before updating on a metered network
Asked when you update by hand while automatic updates wait for an unmetered network. Automatic updates are not changed.
Open the last category at start
Off: the app starts on All. The read filter, period and order are kept either way.

On a wide window the categories can stay open in a pane at the left; the tabs and swiping stay too. Auto shows the pane from 840 dp wide. Pane when possible shows it from 600 dp, if the articles keep enough room. Drawer only always uses the drawer behind the menu button. A narrow window always uses the drawer.
Not available on this Android version. Needs Android 12 or later.
Dynamic is chosen, but this Android version cannot draw it, so Classic is shown. The choice is kept.

Classic is the blue the app has always used. Dynamic takes its colors from the wallpaper (Android 12 and later). Custom makes a light and a dark set from one base color you choose, with text and icon colors the app keeps readable; under Details you can also set five colors of each mode yourself, text included. Photos and icons are never tinted.
Multiplied with the system font size, so a larger system size stays larger.
A sample headline shows how titles look
A short summary line shows how body text looks in this color set and text size.
This layout has no arrangement or column setting.
The Magazine arrangement does not apply to Masonry and Bento; they place their tiles by themselves.
Mixed: cards of different sizes, like a magazine page. Even: the same size for every card.
Choices for a setting that this layout does not have are kept for when the layout changes.
Custom Tabs open the article in a tab of your browser on top of this app. If that is not possible, the external browser is used.
No app on this device can open or save files.

A backup holds your subscriptions, categories with their order, pins and layouts, read and saved state, the articles kept on this device and all settings. Feed icons and the image cache are not included. The file is not encrypted: keep it somewhere private.
Restoring replaces all current Folirel data with the contents of a backup. You see what the backup holds before anything changes.
The backup could not be written. Nothing was saved; try another location.
Checking the backup. Nothing is changed yet.
This file is not a Folirel backup. An OPML file is read with Import OPML.
This backup was made by a newer version of Folirel. Update the app to restore it.
This file is larger than a Folirel backup can be.
This file contains unexpected or unsafe entries and is not restored.
This backup is damaged or incomplete.
This backup contains inconsistent data and is not restored.
The file could not be read.
Restoring replaces all current Folirel data on this device with this backup: subscriptions, categories, articles, read and saved state and settings.
Now on this device: feeds %1$d, articles %2$d, saved %3$d.
No feed is fetched during the restore or right after it. Feeds are updated by your next manual or automatic update.
The current subscriptions, articles, read and saved state and settings are replaced by the backup. This cannot be undone.
Your data and settings are as they were in the backup. Feeds are updated by your next update.
An update or the HTTPS check is still running. Try again in a moment. Nothing was changed.
The backup could not be restored. Your data and settings were not changed.
The backup could not be restored. Your data was not changed; your previous settings are put back when Folirel starts next time.
